oop-classes.summary: Know how attribute lookup, method binding and the MRO really work, and how dataclasses, enums, ABCs and class-creation hooks build on them.
points: Class attributes are shared; assigning through an instance (even with `+=`) creates an instance attribute that shadows the class one.
Functions become bound methods via the descriptor protocol; every access creates a new bound method, so compare with `==`, not `is`.
The MRO comes from C3 linearization: subclasses before bases, declared base order preserved, or a TypeError if impossible.
`super()` means the next class in the MRO of the instance, so cooperative `__init__` methods must forward `**kwargs`.
dataclass rejects mutable defaults, orders fields with defaults last, removes `__hash__` unless frozen, and builds a new class for `slots=True`.
Enum members are singletons; duplicate values create aliases, and plain Enum never equals its raw value (IntEnum and StrEnum do).
Prefer `__init_subclass__` and class decorators to metaclasses; reach for a metaclass only to control `__call__`, `__prepare__` or class creation itself.
traps: A class that defines `__eq__` without `__hash__` becomes unhashable.
Implicit dunder calls such as `len(proxy)` bypass `__getattr__`, so delegation proxies must define those methods explicitly.
Zero-argument `super()` needs the compiler-made `__class__` cell, so it fails in functions attached after class creation and in `@dataclass(slots=True)` methods on 3.13.
